Picks a segment → the next video names it back

The quiz asks “Which One Best Describes You?” with options like I'm a founder, coach, or consultant. Brunson's VIP video then opens “on the last page you told me that you are a bootstrap founder or CEO, kind of like me”. Segmentation captured before the email, and spoken back inside the very next asset. Cheap, and it makes a recording feel addressed to one person.

VERIFIED · quiz walked and VIP video transcribed 31 Jul
Registers → VIP given away at $0

$97 struck to $0 on a 20-minute timer. Jordan Lee and Miss Affiliate both charge $27 for the identical slot. Brunson is buying attendance and commitment, not front-end cash, because the money lands on day five. Show rate is the metric he is optimising — the same one we are.

VERIFIED · captured on the VIP page 31 Jul
Phone captured under an AI-caller consent

The form field is literally named aisc_bot_calling_checkbox and the label covers “automated calls, including prerecorded or AI-generated voice messages”. Their own copy says consent is not required to attend, so it was left unticked and registration still completed.

VERIFIED · form inspected and submitted unticked 31 Jul
The sessions are genuinely live

Unlike Richard Yu and Karla Marie, nothing static is exposed. Zoom is WebRTC, so the scheduled sniffer will report “needs a human”. Price, offer stack and the day-five close are all unobserved until someone attends or a replay is posted.
